To preserve accuracy at such a low bit-width, a mixed-precision strategy is used: only the modules that dominate the parameter count are quantized to 4 bit, while precision-sensitive modules fall back to higher precision or are not quantized at all.

Module  | Quantization configuration
--- | ---
MoE FFN routed experts  | W4A4 MXFP4
Attention linear layers  | W8A8 MXFP8
FFN shared experts  | W8A8 MXFP8
Router gates, compressor projections (`wgate`/`wkv`), indexer projections, and MTP layers  | Not quantized (kept in high precision)

  * Quantization algorithm: The weights and activations use the MXFP4/MXFP8 microscaling formats. Each tensor is divided into blocks of 32 elements, and each block shares a single scaling factor obtained with symmetric min-max calibration on a mixed calibration dataset. Block-wise scaling adapts to the local dynamic range of each tensor, so the quantization error is far lower than that of uniform INT4 quantization.
  * C8 (FP8 KV cache): C8 is a dynamic quantization applied to the KV cache during inference. On 950PR&950DT products, the KV cache is quantized to FP8 (not INT8). It is unrelated to the parameters stored in the weight checkpoint and is controlled only by the serving configuration. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro share exactly the same C8 scheme:
    * Attention KV cache (FP8 by default on 950PR&950DT products; switch back to BF16 with `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`): the compressed KV latent, which serves as both K and V, is dynamically quantized per 64-element tile to FP8 (E4M3) with a shared E8M0 scale per tile; the RoPE part of the KV cache stays in BF16, and Q is not quantized.
    * Indexer cache (enabled with `--attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8`): both indexer Q and K are first rotated by a Hadamard matrix to spread outliers, and then dynamically quantized per token to FP8 (E4M3) with per-token FP32 scales.

For W4A4C8 accuracy scores, see Accuracy Evaluation.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## v0.30.0 - 2026.10.29

This is the stable release of vLLM Ascend v0.30.0, built on the v0.29 release line and aligned with upstream vLLM v0.30.0 via the main2main pipeline. Building on v0.30.0rc1, this release integrates FlashMLA decode with DCP and DSpark, extends KV Pool layerwise pooling and PCP speculative decoding, hardens EPLB for the new quantization formats, and fixes the stability issues across attention, MoE, KV transfer, and Model Runner V2 execution reported during the RC cycle. It still focuses on the flagship models: DeepSeek V4.1, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek V4-Flash/Pro, Kimi K3. Model or hardware combinations outside the scope declared in v0.30.0 are not part of the release claims. Please follow the official documentation to get started.

PR references marked with † were merged into the v0.30.0 release branch before v0.30.0rc1.

> Notice: In this version, modelrunner still defaults to v1, but some models require v2 to be enabled for support. For specific information, please refer to the model tutorial. We plan to fully switch to Model Runner V2 in the next version.

### Highlights

  * DeepSeek V4.1: Added DeepSeek V4.1 support on Model Runner V2, enabled torch.compile, and sped up startup via in-place rotary embedding, reused filtered RoPE lookups, and removed redundant DSV4.1 indexer/SP copies; added the TurboQuant 4-bit latent KV cache for DSA sparse models (DeepSeek V4 Flash; A2/A3 only), including packed KV cache in the V1 runner; fixed ModelSlim-quantized DSV4 weight layout and added AscendStore preparation for V4.1, and packaged attention operators (QLI/QSLI/MQSMLA) with DSL.   * Qwen3.8-27B: Supported non-contiguous KV cache in hybrid linear-attention models, respected per-layer KV cache dtype and kept KV cache contiguous for paged attention, restored C8 V scales on hybrid cache page reassignment, restored Mamba block tables before deferred PP postprocessing, added the FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill, and fixed 310P performance and kernel compatibility for quantized deployment. #14340 #17924 #18003 #17956 #17954 #17565 #17534 #16420 #17964 #17278†
  * Kimi K3 on Ascend: Added end-to-end Kimi K3 support, including MLA DSpark speculative decoding, no-RoPE MLAPO on Ascend 950, fused QKV projections, fused norm gate and attention residual, EPLB, MegaMoE, and projector rotation. #12950 #13277 #13507 #13989 #13509 #14231†
  * GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 / DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 accuracy and performance: Resolved GLM-5.2 DSpark acceptance regressions and DeepSeek V4 Flash-0731 / Pro-0813 accuracy issues (reasoning-effort alignment, routed SwiGLU limit, and frontend behavior), and reused DSV4 compressor metadata across layers for better performance. #12262 #13531 #13993 #14074 #14397 #14624 #14994†
  * Deprecation cleanup: Removed layer sharding, FlashComm2, multistream overlap gate, dynamic-batch SLO, weight prefetch, matmul all-reduce fusions, and kv offload in KV Pool to streamline the codebase. #11953 #12117 #11956 #11933 #11949 #12119 #11904†
  * FlashMLA decode: Integrated FlashMLA decode with DCP and DSpark, routed strided MLA cache writes through PROLOG_V3, used native GatherPa for strided MLA cache reads, enabled no-RoPE MLAPO for token-fused FlashMLA, and skipped FlashMLA CPU length synchronization under DCP. #18758 #18682 #19151 #19155 #19115 #19038
  * KV Pool: Added global layer-window prefetch for layerwise loads, GLM-5.3-Flash Mooncake layerwise support, and Triton KeyPool cache adapters; supported packed SFA C8 layerwise transfer, and reduced lookup/reachable-mask and page-table overhead. #18975 #18749 #18296 #18716 #18837 #18576 #18245
  * MoE: Backported Kimi K3 MegaMoE routed dimensions, integrated the `mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla` operator for the DeepSeek-V4 FP8 KV path, fused shared W8A8 MXFP activation quantization, and used BF16 router GEMM with FP32 accumulation. #18976 #18808 #18678 #18820
  * PCP & speculative decoding: Supported PCP with PIECEWISE and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, fixed-K speculative decode request sharding in PCP, and speculative decoding in KVPP. #18365 #18312 #18334
  * EPLB: Supported Kimi K3 and its MTP draft model and w8a8_mxfp8 on A5, and hardened staging-buffer fencing, HIXL registration ranges, and expert weight updates. #18261 [#18436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascen...

## v0.30.0rc2

v0.30.0rc2

Pre-release

Compare

### Features

  * Added DeepSeek V4.1 support on Model Runner V2, with AscendStore preparation for V4.1. #16899 #16973
  * Extended Model Runner V2 with fine-grained TP (MLP, embedding, o_proj in graph mode) and async CPP scheduling. #17361 #16967 #17380
  * Added the TurboQuant 4-bit latent KV cache for SFA (GLM-5.2/5.3) and DSA (DeepSeek V4 Flash; A2/A3 only) and extended the packed KV cache to the V1 runner; added DeepSeek V4.1 PCP support, GQA PCP and DCP stacking, and graph execution for sharded decode requests in PCP. #18048 #17992 #18066 #18196
  * Enabled sparse SFA C8 (INT8 packed KV cache) for GLM-5.3-Flash, and supported C8-MXFP (FP8 KV cache with E8M0 scales) and INT8 C8 RoPE0 on A2/A3. #17180 #16706
  * Added KV Pool support for GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise pooling and Mamba in Mooncake layerwise, plus layerwise memcache DRAM/SSD pooling. #16945 #17287 #17698
### Performance

Unless stated otherwise, these optimizations are selected automatically for the targeted path and need no additional configuration.

  * Optimized MiniMax-M3 MSA index-score computation for prefill, decode, and speculative decode. #14539
  * Reworked MiniMax-M3 decode score computation and TP communication to exchange index queries and local top-k candidates instead of full index KV data. #13142
  * Reduced the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention score operator cost and added FlashDecoding support. #13987
  * Overlapped shared-expert input/output collectives and projections with routed-expert computation in the supported MoE multistream path. #15974
  * Built DeepSeek V4 compressor, indexer, sparse-attention, and DSpark metadata asynchronously on eligible Model Runner V1 paths. #15776
  * Improved DeepSeek V4 DSA-CP prefill execution by aligning sequence parallelism with the model and attention collectives. #16021
  * Prefetched two AscendStore layers by default to reduce layerwise KV Pool stalls. #15797

### Dependencies

Use the official v0.27.1rc1 release images to ensure that the required operator packages and matching dependency versions are installed.

  * Upstream vLLM: v0.27.1.
  * Python: >= 3.10, < 3.13; the release images use Python 3.12.
  * Ascend HDK: 26.1.1.
  * CANN: 9.1.0.
  * PTA (PyTorch / torch_npu): 2.10.0 / 2.10.0.post4.
  * Triton Ascend: 3.2.2.
  * Mooncake: 0.3.11.post1 in the release images.

### Deprecation and Configuration Changes

  * The parameters `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` and `enable_sparse_li_c8` will be deprecated in a future release. For KV cache quantization, we have aligned the configuration approach with the upstream community. Use `--kv-cache-dtype` and `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype` to specify quantization types.

The corresponding Ascend PLOG reports:
    
    `[kv_rms_norm_rope_cache_base_tiling.cpp:439][OPS_BASE][GetShapeAttrsInfo]

#### Root cause

The draft model and draft attention metadata use two different token counts during uneven DP execution:

  * The model executes `batch_desc.num_tokens`, which includes the DP-synchronized padding row (four rows in this example).
  * Upstream draft attention metadata is deliberately built from the real query count, effectively `batch_desc.num_reqs or num_reqs` (three rows here).
  * The SFA RoPE/KV-cache path applies `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache` directly to the full model tensor without removing the DP-only row, while `cos`, `sin`, and cache slots come from the three-row attention metadata.

#### Expected behavior

SFA draft execution should handle uneven DP batches without passing inconsistent token dimensions to `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache`. DP-only model padding must not be processed as a real attention query/cache write, and the returned attention output must retain the model tensor's padded shape expected by the surrounding execution path.
